text: Read Source A and then answer the questions below.
The British Social Attitudes (BSA) survey studies public opinion on social and political issues in
Britain. The survey has been done each year since 1983. Researchers interview participants in
their homes using a structured interview with 300 closed pre-coded questions. The questions in
the survey ask about issues such as welfare benefits, health care, education, transport, the
Participants are selected for the survey using random sampling. The population of Britain is
approximately 67 million people. The sample for the survey is 4000 adults who live in Britain.
A key aim of the BSA survey is to study changes in public opinion on social and political issues
over time, so some questions are the same and repeated every year. Other questions in the survey
The BSA survey collects quantitative data and produces statistics. These statistics make the survey
useful for both government policy making and sociologists doing research.
